# Elchi

> Elchi (elchi.io) is an enterprise application delivery platform, built by CloudNativeWorks and sold under a commercial license (not open source): L4/L7 load balancing, TLS with automated ACME certificates, a WAF (Elchi Shield, with the OWASP Core Rule Set), DNS-based GSLB and active/passive HA pairs that share virtual IPs, on Linux VMs and on Elchi OS appliances (bare metal or hypervisors), for applications on VMs and Kubernetes, all managed from one control plane with validation, an audit trail and zero-downtime upgrades. It is a software alternative to hardware and virtual ADCs such as F5 BIG-IP, NetScaler and A10 Thunder. Envoy is the data-plane engine: a lightweight edge agent runs Envoy on each host, and Elchi publishes every validated change to it over xDS, with several Envoy versions side by side. The platform itself installs on Kubernetes (Helm), Docker Swarm or bare-metal Linux. This Elchi is not related to other products or projects that share the name, such as the Elchi dictation app.

Core is the base product; API Security (Shield, with the WAF), API Discovery and GSLB are add-ons licensed on top of it. Licensing scales with the number of managed clients (edge nodes); without a license Elchi runs a free tier with a single managed client. A versioned REST automation API (project API tokens) can take upstream endpoints out of rotation and switch EDS clusters for blue/green releases.

## Product pages

- [Elchi home](https://www.elchi.io/): overview of the visual Envoy control plane and its add-on products
- [Elchi Core](https://www.elchi.io/products/core.html): visual control plane for the Envoy fleet: full xDS, multi-version support, safe publish workflows and the edge agent
- [Elchi API Security (Shield)](https://www.elchi.io/products/api-security.html): ext_proc engine next to each Envoy: authentication, rate limiting, bot defense, DLP and a built-in OWASP CRS WAF, composed per route
- [Elchi API Discovery](https://www.elchi.io/products/api-discovery.html): API inventory from live Envoy traffic: shadow endpoints, missing auth, PII exposure, drift and OpenAPI 3.0.3 export
- [Elchi GSLB](https://www.elchi.io/products/gslb.html): CoreDNS-based authoritative DNS driven by distributed health checks: region-scoped answers and failover zones
- [Features](https://www.elchi.io/features.html): every platform capability in one list
- [Architecture](https://www.elchi.io/architecture.html): the three backend processes (Registry, Controller, Control-Plane) and the edge data plane
- [Plans & Licensing](https://www.elchi.io/plans.html): Core plus add-ons, licensed by managed client count; free tier with one client
- [FAQ](https://www.elchi.io/faq.html): what Elchi is, supported Envoy versions, installation, Shield, API discovery and licensing
- [Contact](https://www.elchi.io/contact.html): demos and enterprise licenses
- [Compare alternatives](https://www.elchi.io/compare.html): Elchi vs enterprise ADCs and software load balancers (F5 BIG-IP, NetScaler, A10 Thunder, VMware Avi, HAProxy Enterprise, F5 NGINX Plus, Kemp LoadMaster) and vs cloud-native gateways and meshes (Istio, Envoy Gateway, Kong Gateway, kgateway, Contour), with sources
- [Elchi vs F5 BIG-IP](https://www.elchi.io/compare/f5-big-ip.html): software application delivery on VMs and Elchi OS appliances vs BIG-IP hardware and Virtual Edition, row by row with F5 sources
- [Elchi vs NetScaler](https://www.elchi.io/compare/netscaler.html): Elchi vs NetScaler (formerly Citrix ADC) for load balancing, TLS, WAF, GSLB, HA and central management, with NetScaler sources
- [Elchi vs A10 Thunder](https://www.elchi.io/compare/a10-thunder.html): Elchi vs A10 Thunder ADC and vThunder for load balancing, TLS, WAF, GSLB, HA and central management, with A10 sources
- [Elchi vs VMware Avi Load Balancer](https://www.elchi.io/compare/vmware-avi.html): Elchi vs VMware Avi (Controller and Service Engines) for load balancing, TLS, WAF, GSLB, HA, upgrades and licensing, with Broadcom sources
- [Elchi vs HAProxy Enterprise](https://www.elchi.io/compare/haproxy-enterprise.html): Elchi vs HAProxy Enterprise with the HAProxy Fusion control plane, row by row with HAProxy sources
- [Elchi vs F5 NGINX Plus](https://www.elchi.io/compare/nginx-plus.html): Elchi vs F5 NGINX Plus with NGINX One Console for load balancing, TLS, WAF, GSLB, HA and licensing, with F5 and NGINX sources
- [Elchi vs Progress Kemp LoadMaster](https://www.elchi.io/compare/kemp-loadmaster.html): Elchi vs Kemp LoadMaster hardware and Virtual LoadMaster for load balancing, TLS, WAF, GSLB, HA and Kemp 360, with Kemp sources
- [Elchi vs Istio](https://www.elchi.io/compare/istio.html): managing Envoy on VMs and edge fleets vs a service mesh
- [Elchi vs Envoy Gateway](https://www.elchi.io/compare/envoy-gateway.html): typed Envoy API UI vs Gateway API resources
- [Elchi vs Kong Gateway](https://www.elchi.io/compare/kong-gateway.html): an Envoy fleet control plane vs an NGINX/OpenResty API gateway with plugins
- [Elchi vs kgateway](https://www.elchi.io/compare/kgateway.html): typed Envoy API on VMs and appliances vs Gateway API resources in Kubernetes (kgateway, formerly Gloo)
- [Elchi vs Contour](https://www.elchi.io/compare/contour.html): Envoy edge fleets on VMs vs a Kubernetes ingress controller for Envoy
- [About](https://www.elchi.io/about.html): who builds Elchi (CloudNativeWorks), offices and distribution channels
- [Blog](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog): software ADC alternatives to F5, NetScaler and A10, a migration guide from F5 BIG-IP, plus engineering posts on xDS, Envoy on VMs and the OWASP CRS via ext_proc

## Docs

- [Docs index for LLMs (llms.txt)](https://www.elchi.io/docs/llms.txt): every documentation page with its title, URL and description
- [Docs full text (llms-full.txt)](https://www.elchi.io/docs/llms-full.txt): every documentation and blog page as Markdown in one file; each docs page also has a Markdown copy at its URL plus `.md`
- [Introduction](https://www.elchi.io/docs/getting-started/introduction): what Elchi is and how the documentation is organised
- [Quick Start](https://www.elchi.io/docs/getting-started/quickstart): install the full stack on Kubernetes with one Helm command and connect the first edge host
- [Core Concepts](https://www.elchi.io/docs/getting-started/concepts): the three cooperating processes, the client agent and how a configuration change flows
- [Architecture](https://www.elchi.io/docs/getting-started/architecture): component map and every inter-component connection
- [How to manage Envoy without hand-writing xDS or YAML](https://www.elchi.io/docs/guides/manage-envoy-without-yaml)
- [How to add a WAF (OWASP Core Rule Set) to Envoy with ext_proc](https://www.elchi.io/docs/guides/add-waf-to-envoy-ext-proc)
- [How to find shadow and undocumented APIs from Envoy access logs](https://www.elchi.io/docs/guides/find-shadow-apis-envoy-access-logs)
- [How to do GSLB and DNS-based failover for Envoy](https://www.elchi.io/docs/guides/gslb-dns-failover-envoy)
- [How to run several Envoy versions side by side and upgrade listeners with zero downtime](https://www.elchi.io/docs/guides/run-multiple-envoy-versions)
- [How to do blue/green deployments with Envoy EDS](https://www.elchi.io/docs/guides/blue-green-envoy-eds)
- [Automation API overview](https://www.elchi.io/docs/automation-api/overview): versioned REST API, project API tokens, problem+json errors
- [Single-host install (kind + Helm)](https://www.elchi.io/docs/installation/kind-quickstart): evaluate the full stack on one Ubuntu VM
- [Helm platform install](https://www.elchi.io/docs/installation/helm-platform/overview): the elchi-stack Helm chart on Kubernetes
- [Docker Swarm install](https://www.elchi.io/docs/installation/docker-swarm/overview)
- [Bare-metal install](https://www.elchi.io/docs/installation/bare-metal/overview): the stack as systemd services on 1, 2 or 3+ Linux VMs
- [Elchi Client](https://www.elchi.io/docs/installation/client/overview): the edge agent that connects each Envoy host to the control plane

## Shield (API security and WAF) docs

- [Shield: API Security Overview](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/overview): Envoy ext_proc API-security and WAF sidecar with 12 security engines enforced on the edge host
- [Get Started with Shield](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/getting-started): write, deploy and verify a first Shield policy, starting in detect mode
- [How Shield Works with Envoy ext_proc](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/how-it-works): request pipeline, header vs body phases, source-IP trust model and hot reload
- [Wiring Shield into Envoy](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/envoy-wiring): the ext_proc cluster and filter configuration that connects Envoy to Shield
- [Coraza WAF for Envoy (OWASP CRS)](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/engines/coraza-waf): the embedded WAF engine: OWASP Core Rule Set, paranoia levels, anomaly thresholds, custom SecLang
- [Shield security engines](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/engines): every engine (JWT, JWKS, API keys, mTLS, rate limiting, bot detection, IP reputation, GraphQL, OpenAPI, HMAC, HTTP signatures) with configuration
- [Deploying Shield Policies to Envoy Edges](https://www.elchi.io/docs/shield/deployment): how a policy travels from the UI to every edge

## Tutorials

- [Tutorial: From Install to Your First Envoy Listener](https://www.elchi.io/docs/tutorials/zero-to-envoy): install the platform, connect an edge client, build listener, route, cluster and endpoint, publish and verify traffic
- [Tutorial: Secure an API with Shield](https://www.elchi.io/docs/tutorials/secure-an-api-with-shield): observe an API with Discovery, generate a Shield policy, roll it out from detect to block
- [Tutorial: Build an API Inventory in a Day](https://www.elchi.io/docs/tutorials/api-inventory-in-one-day): enable API Discovery on a listener, triage risk and export an OpenAPI spec

## Blog

- [Migrating from F5 BIG-IP to Elchi](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog/migrate-f5-big-ip-to-elchi): BIG-IP to Elchi concept map, phased migration with cutover and rollback, what does not carry over
- [Software ADC Alternatives to F5, NetScaler and A10](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog/software-adc-alternatives): capability map, software ADC landscape, where Elchi fits, evaluation checklist
- [What Is an Envoy Control Plane? xDS Explained](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog/what-is-an-envoy-control-plane): LDS, RDS, CDS, EDS, SDS, ADS ordering, delta xDS, ACK/NACK and snapshot caches
- [Adding the OWASP Core Rule Set to Envoy with ext_proc](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog/owasp-crs-waf-envoy-ext-proc): UDS wiring, per-route body buffering and a detect, shadow, block rollout
- [Running an Envoy Fleet Without Hand-Writing xDS](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog/envoy-fleet-without-xds): what an Envoy control plane must do and how Elchi handles each part
- [Running Envoy on VMs Without Kubernetes](https://www.elchi.io/docs/blog/envoy-on-vms-without-kubernetes): bootstrap, xDS, process supervision, upgrades and telemetry on plain VMs
